cron.description: 6-field Quartz cron (Second Minute Hour DayOfMonth Month DayOfWeek)

digest_url.description: URL fetched on every firing. It lives in the schedule's emit_body tool_call args, so an instance retunes it with an `override_params` entry naming `schedules` -- the whole list, last-write-wins.

chat_id.description: Target chat of a SCHEDULED digest, as a string, stamped on the schedule's emit_headers and promoted into context by the out-edge. It ships EMPTY: under the environment form an unset chat id refused the boot and named the variable, and a params default cannot refuse. What replaces that refusal is the template's own shape -- the hive instantiates INACTIVE, so nothing fires until a crossing edge is drawn, and the mutation that draws it is the one that names the chat. An empty chat id delivers nowhere rather than somewhere wrong.

description.purpose: Fires the daily-digest schedule: one tool_call body carrying the digest URL, plus the chat_id header for delivery routing.
description.use_when: Inside the daily-digest pipeline; runtime schedule changes arrive as op messages (add/modify/remove by schedule_id).
description.not_in_scope: No content generation — the timer sends exactly what the schedule's emit_body declares. Missed firings are dropped, not replayed.
description.emits_meaning: messages[]: the schedule's static tool_call ({url}) for the fetcher. hop: timer-automatic fields (event_id/schedule_id/schedule_name/scheduled_at/fired_at/iteration_n) plus chat_id from emit_headers (string — recast to number by the format cell).
description.consumes_meaning: op messages per the timer cell convention (add/modify/remove with schedule_id as the key; once-vs-repeating may not be switched by modify).
examples: 08:00:00 -> emit { messages: [tool_call {url: <params.digest_url>}] }, hop { schedule_name: 'daily-digest', chat_id: '<digest chat>' }
